hook.en: "The treatment did not work overall, but it worked in women over 50 with a history of knee pain on Tuesdays." Sound ridiculous? A chart of 20 tests will produce one "significant" result by chance alone. Learn how to spot findings that were dug out of the data, and how to avoid doing it.
hook.ur: "Ilaaj ne kul mila kar kaam nahi kiya, lekin 50 se zyada umar ki khawateen mein jinhein ghutne ke dard ki tareekh thi mangal ko kaam kiya." Bejaa lagta hai? 20 tests ka chart sirf ittifaq se ek "significant" nateeja paida kar dega. Seekhein ke data se khod kar nikaale gaye findings kaise pehchanein, aur khud aisa karne se kaise bachein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain why many tests make false positives likely, judge a subgroup claim with five questions, tell planned from post-hoc analyses, and name ways to avoid p-hacking such as pre-registration and correcting for multiple comparisons.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke bohat se tests jhoote positive ka imkaan kyun barhate hain, subgroup ke daawe ko paanch sawalon se parkhenge, planned ko post-hoc analyses se alag karenge, aur p-hacking se bachne ke tareeqe jaise pre-registration aur multiple comparisons ki correction batayenge.

text.en: With a 5 percent significance level, each test has a 1 in 20 chance of a false positive when there is truly no effect. Run 20 independent tests and you expect one false "hit"; the chance of at least one is about 64 percent. **Subgroup analyses** (splitting patients by age, sex or severity) multiply the number of tests. **P-hacking** means trying different analyses, outcomes, cut-offs or exclusions until p falls below 0.05, and reporting only the winner. The antidote is a **pre-specified plan**, and a correction for multiple tests such as **Bonferroni** (divide the threshold by the number of tests).
text.ur: 5 fisad significance level par har test ke jhoote positive ka 20 mein se 1 imkaan hota hai jab waqai koi asar na ho. 20 azaad tests chalayein to ek jhoote "hit" ki tawaqqo hoti hai; kam az kam ek ka imkaan takreeban 64 fisad hai. **Subgroup analyses** (mareezon ko umar, jins ya shiddat se baantna) tests ki ginti barhate hain. **P-hacking** ka matlab mukhtalif analyses, nateeje, cut-offs ya exclusions aazmana jab tak p 0.05 se neeche na aaye, aur sirf jeetne wale ko report karna. Tareeqa pehle se tay shuda plan hai, aur multiple tests ki correction jaise **Bonferroni** (had ko tests ki ginti se taqseem).

text.en: Think of **throwing darts at a wall and then painting the target around where they landed**. Anyone can hit a bullseye that way. A real test says where the target is before throwing. Post-hoc subgroup results are targets painted after the throw.
text.ur: **Deewar par teer phenk kar phir jahan lage wahan nishana banana** sochein. Is tarah koi bhi bullseye maar sakta hai. Asal test phenkne se pehle batata hai nishana kahan hai. Post-hoc subgroup nateeje phenkne ke baad banaye gaye nishane hain.

title.en: Five questions for any subgroup claim
title.ur: Kisi bhi subgroup ke daawe ke liye paanch sawal

steps.title: Was it planned in advance?
steps.detail: Look for a pre-specified subgroup in the protocol or registration. Post-hoc subgroups are only hypotheses. || Kya pehle se plan tha?

steps.title: Was there a test of interaction?
steps.detail: The right test asks whether the treatment effect differs between subgroups, not whether it was significant in one and not in the other. || Kya interaction ka test tha?

steps.title: How many subgroups were examined?
steps.detail: If 20 were tested, one or two "significant" results are expected by chance. || Kitne subgroups dekhe gaye?

steps.title: Is there a biological or clinical reason?
steps.detail: A subgroup with a plausible mechanism is more believable than a random split. || Kya haqeeqi ya clinical wajah hai?

steps.title: Has it been replicated?
steps.detail: A subgroup finding in one trial should be confirmed in another before changing practice. || Kya dohraya gaya?

question.en: A trial of exercise for neck pain is negative overall, but the abstract highlights a significant benefit in left-handed women under 35 (p = 0.04). The protocol did not list this subgroup. How should you treat it?
question.ur: Gardan dard ke liye exercise ka trial kul mila kar manfi hai, lekin abstract 35 se kam umar ki left-handed khawateen mein significant faida (p = 0.04) numaya karta hai. Protocol mein yeh subgroup nahi tha. Is se kaise nibtein?

text.en: As a hypothesis for future research, not a finding to act on, since it was post-hoc, among many possible splits
text.ur: Mustaqbil ki research ke liye hypothesis ke taur par, amal ke liye finding nahi, kyunke yeh post-hoc tha, bohat se mumkina baanton mein se

feedback.en: Yes — post-hoc subgroups are likely chance findings.
feedback.ur: Haan — post-hoc subgroups ke ittifaqi findings hone ka imkaan zyada hai.

text.en: As proof that left-handed women benefit
text.ur: Is saboot ke taur par ke left-handed khawateen ko faida hota hai

feedback.en: It is probably an honest chance finding.
feedback.ur: Yeh shayad imaandar ittifaqi finding hai.

question.en: A researcher runs 20 separate tests, each at p < 0.05. Roughly how likely is at least one false-positive result if no real effects exist?
question.ur: Muhaqqiq 20 alag tests chalata hai, har ek p < 0.05 par. Agar koi asal asar na ho to kam az kam ek jhoote positive nateeje ka imkaan takreeban kitna hai?

feedback.en: Yes — 1 minus 0.95 to the power of 20 is about 0.64.
feedback.ur: Haan — 1 minus 0.95 ki taqat 20 takreeban 0.64 hai.

feedback.en: The chance is much higher than that.
feedback.ur: Imkaan is se kahin zyada hai.

feedback.en: That is for a single test.
feedback.ur: Yeh ek test ke liye hai.

question.en: Which is the best way to prevent p-hacking in your own project?
question.ur: Apne project mein p-hacking rokne ka behtareen tareeqa kaun sa hai?

text.en: Write and register a protocol with one primary outcome and a planned analysis before collecting data
text.ur: Data jama karne se pehle ek primary outcome aur planned analysis ke saath protocol likh kar register karein

feedback.en: Yes — pre-specification stops choosing after the fact.
feedback.ur: Haan — pehle se tay karna baad mein chunne se rokta hai.

text.en: Try several analyses and pick the clearest
text.ur: Kai analyses aazmayein aur sab se saaf chunein

text.en: Remove outliers until the result is significant
text.ur: Outliers tab tak hatayein jab tak nateeja significant na ho

text.en: **Calling exploratory findings confirmed.** Exploring data is fine; the sin is reporting exploration as if it were a plan. Label analyses clearly as pre-specified or exploratory. Another trap is the "significant here, not there" fallacy: showing a benefit in men (p = 0.03) and none in women (p = 0.20) does not show a difference between them. Also, do not drop results that did not work: report every outcome you measured.
text.ur: **Tajrabaati findings ko tasdeeq shuda kehna.** Data ko khangalna theek hai; gunah tajrabe ki report ko plan ki tarah pesh karna hai. Analyses ko saaf taur par pehle se tay shuda ya tajrabaati likhein. Ek aur jaal "yahan significant, wahan nahi" ki ghalat fehmi hai: mardon mein faida (p = 0.03) aur khawateen mein nahi (p = 0.20) dikhane ka matlab yeh nahi ke un mein farq hai. Un nateejon ko bhi na chhodein jo kaam nahi kiye: har naapa gaya nateeja report karein.

text.en: **Be a sceptical, kind reader.** When a colleague excitedly shares a subgroup result, ask: "Was that planned? How many groups did they look at?" Without dismissing, say: "Interesting idea, let us see if it holds up." In your own audits, decide the question and the analysis first, and tell everyone what you looked at, including what you did not find.
text.ur: **Shak karne wale lekin naram parhne wale banein.** Jab koi saathi josh se subgroup ka nateeja share kare to poochhein: "Kya yeh plan tha? Kitne groups dekhe?" Radd kiye baghair kahein: "Dilchasp khayal hai, dekhte hain tika rehta hai ya nahi." Apne audits mein pehle sawal aur analysis tay karein, aur sab ko batayein ke aap ne kya dekha, jo nahi mila woh bhi.

question.en: Is looking at subgroups always wrong?
question.ur: Kya subgroups dekhna hamesha ghalat hai?

answer.en: No. Pre-planned subgroups with a plausible reason and a proper test of interaction are legitimate, for example whether a treatment works differently in older and younger people. Exploratory subgroup analyses are also valuable for generating hypotheses. The error is claiming a post-hoc finding as established, or hiding how many analyses were run.
answer.ur: Nahi. Pehle se plan shuda subgroups jin ki munasib wajah ho aur interaction ka sahi test ho jaiz hain, masalan kya ilaaj buzurgon aur jawanon mein mukhtalif kaam karta hai. Tajrabaati subgroup analyses hypotheses paida karne ke liye bhi qeemti hain. Ghalti post-hoc finding ko qaim shuda kehna, ya chhupana hai ke kitne analyses chalaye gaye.

beats.patient: A group reports that a new shoulder programme "works best in diabetics" after testing nine patient characteristics and finding a significant interaction only for diabetes (p = 0.03).
beats.assessment: Nine characteristics were tested, so about one false positive is expected; the subgroup was not planned.
beats.treatment: She notes that with a Bonferroni threshold of 0.05 divided by 9 (0.006), the result is not significant, and describes it as exploratory.
beats.reassess: Her talk says the result is an idea worth testing in a new trial, and she does not tell patients that diabetics benefit more.

text.en: **Do not change care for patients on a subgroup claim.** Withholding a helpful treatment from a group because of a chance finding, or giving a risky treatment to a group because "it worked for them", can cause real harm. Wait for replication, especially for safety-critical decisions.
text.ur: **Subgroup ke daawe par mareezon ki care na badlein.** Ittifaqi finding ki wajah se kisi group se mufeed ilaaj rok dena, ya kisi group ko khatarnak ilaaj dena kyunke "unke liye kaam kiya", asal nuqsan kar sakta hai. Dohrane ka intezar karein, khaaskar safety ke ahem faislon mein.

text.en: Wang and colleagues in the New England Journal of Medicine described the problem of subgroup analyses in clinical trials, advising that investigators should state subgroups in advance, report how many were examined, use tests of interaction and treat the results as hypothesis-generating. Head and colleagues examined p-values across many scientific fields and found evidence of p-hacking, with an excess of p-values just below 0.05, although they judged that its effect on broad conclusions was probably weak.
text.ur: Wang aur saathiyon ne New England Journal of Medicine mein clinical trials mein subgroup analyses ke masle ko bayan kiya, mashwara diya ke muhaqqiq subgroups pehle se batayein, report karein kitne dekhe gaye, interaction ke tests istemal karein aur nateejon ko hypothesis-paida karne wala samjhein. Head aur saathiyon ne kai science ke shobon mein p-values ka jaiza liya aur p-hacking ka saboot paya, 0.05 se thora neeche p-values ki zyadti ke saath, halaanke unhon ne andaaza lagaya ke wasi nateejon par iska asar shayad kamzor hai.

text.en: **Plan, Interaction, Count, Reason, Repeat.** Was it planned, tested for interaction, how many were counted, is there a reason, and has it been repeated?
text.ur: **Plan, Interaction, Ginti, Wajah, Dohrana.** Kya plan tha, interaction test hua, kitne ginay gaye, wajah hai, aur dohraya gaya?

summary.en: Many tests make false positives likely: 20 tests at the 5 percent level give about a 64 percent chance of at least one.
summary.ur: Bohat se tests jhoote positive ka imkaan barhate hain: 5 fisad level par 20 tests kam az kam ek ka takreeban 64 fisad imkaan dete hain.

summary.en: Judge subgroup claims by whether they were planned, tested for interaction, counted, plausible and replicated.
summary.ur: Subgroup daawon ko is se parkhein ke plan tha, interaction test hua, ginay gaye, munasib hain aur dohraye gaye.

summary.en: Prevent p-hacking by pre-specifying one primary outcome and reporting everything you measured.
summary.ur: P-hacking roken: ek primary outcome pehle se tay karein aur jo naapa sab report karein.

back.en: Trying analyses until p falls below 0.05 and reporting only that one.
back.ur: Analyses tab tak aazmana jab tak p 0.05 se neeche na aaye aur sirf wohi report karna.

front.en: What does the Bonferroni correction do?

back.en: Divides the significance threshold by the number of tests.
back.ur: Significance had ko tests ki ginti se taqseem karti hai.

front.en: Which test judges a subgroup difference?
front.ur: Subgroup farq kaun sa test parakhta hai?

back.en: One decided after seeing the data, so it is hypothesis-generating.
back.ur: Data dekhne ke baad tay kiya gaya, isliye hypothesis-paida karne wala.
